ticket.summary: Customers can check a gift card balance

extra_items.text: Designs are linked, or the ticket says none are needed
extra_items.evidence: Comment from Priya (Product): designs are in Figma (Gift cards / Balance).

extra_items.text: The ticket names the component it changes

criteria.text: Given a valid 16-digit card number and its 4-digit PIN, when the customer selects Check balance, then the balance is shown in AUD with two decimal places and the card's expiry date.
Given a card number that isn't 16 digits, when the customer selects Check balance, then the message "Enter the 16-digit number on the back of your card" is shown and no request is sent to GiftCo.
Given a valid card number and a wrong PIN, when the customer selects Check balance, then the message "The card number or PIN is wrong" is shown and the balance is not shown.

Given 5 wrong PINs for the same card within 15 minutes, when the customer tries again, then balance checks for that card are refused for 15 minutes with the message "Too many attempts. Try again in 15 minutes."
Given GiftCo returns an error or takes longer than 3 seconds, when the customer selects Check balance, then the message "We can't check balances right now. Try again later." is shown.
Given a card with a zero balance, when its balance is checked, then $0.00 is shown with the expiry date.
The balance check returns within 500 ms at p95, measured at our API, excluding GiftCo's response time.

dismissed_flags.reason: "many" is part of the exact error message "Too many attempts. Try again in 15 minutes.", which the criterion quotes as copy; it is not a vague quantity.

dimensions.name: testability
dimensions.rationale: Every criterion has an observable result: a message, a value or a time.
evidence: AC-1 to AC-7 each name what is shown or measured

dimensions.name: clarity
dimensions.rationale: No vague terms remain; the one lint hit is inside quoted copy.

dimensions.name: completeness
dimensions.rationale: Invalid number, wrong PIN, lockout, supplier error or timeout and a zero balance are covered. An expired card is not.

dimensions.name: nfr
dimensions.rationale: The one NFR has a number, a percentile and where it is measured.
evidence: AC-7: 500 ms at p95, measured at our API

dimensions.name: dependencies
dimensions.rationale: The blocking credentials ticket, the supplier API and the designs are named.

dimensions.name: size
dimensions.rationale: One user goal and 7 criteria.

questions.question: What should the customer see when a card has expired but still has a balance?
questions.why: AC-1 shows the expiry date, but no criterion covers an expired card. It may be out of scope; if so, say so.

dependencies.description: Test gift cards with a balance, a zero balance and a known PIN
dependencies.evidence: AC-1, AC-3 and AC-6 need cards in these states; the ticket does not say where they come from

ticket.summary: Customers can apply a discount code in the cart

extra_items.text: Designs are linked, or the ticket says none are needed
extra_items.evidence: No designs are linked; "shown as a separate line" suggests a cart change that needs one.

extra_items.text: The ticket names the component it changes

criteria.text: Given a cart with a subtotal of at least $50, when the customer applies the code SUMMER10, then the subtotal is reduced by 10% and the discount is shown as a separate line.

flags.note: No rounding rule for amounts that are not a whole number of cents.
Nothing says what happens under $50, or when the subtotal drops under $50 later.

criteria.oracle_note: The discount amount can't be checked to the cent until the rounding rule is known.

criteria.text: Given an unknown code, when the customer applies it, then the message "That code isn't valid" is shown and the subtotal is unchanged.
The customer can remove the code, and the subtotal goes back to the original amount.

dimensions.name: testability
dimensions.rationale: Three criteria have a clear result; AC-1 needs a rounding rule.

dimensions.name: clarity
dimensions.rationale: The wording is plain; the one ambiguity is the rounding rule.

dimensions.name: completeness
dimensions.rationale: Stacking, expiry and the under-$50 case are missing.

dimensions.name: nfr
dimensions.rationale: No non-functional need is stated or implied.

dimensions.name: dependencies
dimensions.rationale: The admin tool is named; the test code SUMMER10 must exist in the test environment.
evidence: Description: "created by the promotions team in the admin tool"

dimensions.name: size
dimensions.rationale: One user goal and 4 criteria.

questions.question: Can a customer use SUMMER10 together with another code, such as a members' code? If not, what happens when they apply a second code?
questions.why: A comment from Marketing says a second code might run at the same time. Whether codes stack changes the total.

questions.question: How is the 10% rounded when it is not a whole number of cents (for example on $55.55)?
questions.why: Rounding up, down or to the nearest cent give different totals, so two correct builds would fail each other's tests.

questions.question: When does SUMMER10 expire, and what does the customer see if they apply it after that?
questions.why: A campaign code usually ends; no criterion covers an expired code.

questions.question: What happens if the subtotal drops below $50 after the code is applied, for example when an item is removed?
questions.why: AC-1 sets a $50 minimum but only checks it when the code is applied.

suggestions.suggested: Given a cart with SUMMER10 applied, when the customer applies a second code, then [the second code replaces SUMMER10 | both apply | the second code is rejected with a message].
suggestions.label: suggested

suggestions.original: Given a cart with a subtotal of at least $50, when the customer applies the code SUMMER10, then the subtotal is reduced by 10% and the discount is shown as a separate line.
suggestions.suggested: Given a cart with a subtotal of at least $50, when the customer applies the code SUMMER10, then the subtotal is reduced by 10%, rounded [to the nearest cent], and the discount is shown as a separate line.
suggestions.label: suggested

dependencies.description: SUMMER10 set up in the test environment's admin tool
dependencies.evidence: AC-1 applies SUMMER10; the ticket does not say it exists outside production
